About the Curriculum

Built on Competencies,
Not on Tools

Tools change every year. The ability to think critically, verify information, create responsibly, and act ethically never goes out of date. This curriculum builds those enduring skills — with AI as the partner, never the replacement.

🧠

Human-First Principle

Students think before they prompt. Every activity enforces the sequence: Think → Use AI → Evaluate output.

🌐

6 International Standards

Every competency and outcome is anchored in UNESCO, OECD, DigComp 2.2, ISTE, and UNICEF frameworks.

📐

Constructive Alignment

Objectives → Activities → Assessment → Products form a tight, auditable chain. Rare in AI curriculum design.

🏫

Arabic Classroom Ready

Real scenarios, culturally grounded examples, and differentiation across three grade bands (7–8 · 9–10 · 11–12).

The Learner Journey

Five Stages. One Direction.

The curriculum is structured as a progressive journey — each stage builds on the last, moving students from awareness to action.

01 DISCOVER
AI as Your Learning Companion
KC-1 · AI Awareness
What is AI? How does it differ from search? What are its limits?
02 LEARN
Using AI to Learn Better
KC-2 · AI-Assisted Learning
Prompt engineering. Verification. AI as a study partner.
03 THINK
Can I Trust What AI Tells Me?
KC-3 · Critical Evaluation
Hallucination. Source credibility. Cross-verification framework.
04 CREATE
Using AI to Produce New Work
KC-4 · AI-Enhanced Creation
Co-creation, original voice, and intellectual integrity.
05 ACT
AI Ethics & Responsibility
KC-5 · Ethical Digital Citizenship
Privacy, bias, fairness, and responsible AI citizenship.

Expert Reviews

What Educators Are Saying

Reviewed by curriculum experts, university professors, and ministry officials from across the Arab world.

Outstanding qualitative effort — the kind we have come to expect. The material is excellent, and I read nearly all of it with great enthusiasm. It is clearly appropriate for the target age group, particularly Arab-region students, and could readily be scaled through regional and national institutions. I am ready to help.

م
Dr. Mohammad Matar
Director General, Palestinian National Center — Ministry of Education
ALECSO Advisor for International Assessments · OECD Development Consultant

The curriculum is strong at the level of conceptual design. The philosophical foundation is coherent and substantive — it places the Human-First principle and the procedural sequence (learner thinks first → uses AI → evaluates output) at its core. This translates philosophy into actual pedagogical procedure, which is rare in comparable curricula where philosophy and practice occupy separate worlds.

ه
Dr. Hama Mansour
Director of Planning — Ministry of Education, Egypt

At the level of instructional design, this is professional and coherent work. The Competency Mapping Matrix — linking each unit to its competency, outcomes, assessment tools, and culminating product — gives the curriculum strong constructive alignment, one of the most important quality criteria in curriculum design.

ح
Dr. Hadi Al-Said
Professor of Statistics, University of Tunis · Researcher in Digital Education

All appreciation for this exceptional effort in formulating this integrated system. It transcends abstract theory to offer a promising operational package — a rigorous pedagogical and structural response to the demands of the age, wisely seeking to move the learner from passive technical consumption to building genuine competencies that enshrine the centrality of the human and their informed decision.

ر
Dr. Rifaat Sabbah
Arab Campaign for Education for All (ACEA)

The curriculum is coherent, excellent, and fulfills all curricular elements — from learning outcomes to the alignment matrix, to consistency between activities and outcomes. The work is complete and grounded in modern international references.

ع
Dr. Ali Hussein
Professor of Curriculum and Teaching Methods — Faculty of Education, Al-Azhar University, Cairo
